Hi Ana,

Thanks for starting onboarding with Redwood. We're preparing a purchase order (PROC-4827) to cover the onboarding fee and initial services, but we need to verify tax documentation before we can finalize the PO and set up payments. Please can you send the following so we can complete the vendor record: 

- Completed, signed W-8BEN-E (original signature, date) OR a completed W-9 if you are US-taxable.
- Company registration / certificate of incorporation.
- Government-issued foreign TIN (if you do not have a US EIN) — please indicate the TIN type (e.g., UK UTR) and provide a supporting government letter if available.
- Bank instructions (BACS/SEPA/IBAN) for payment.

If you expect to claim any treaty benefits, please indicate which article and include any supporting documentation. We can accept a notarized W-8BEN-E scan uploaded to the portal or a DocuSign envelope (link below). Once documents are received and validated we will:

1) Clear the vendor in the procurement system,
2) Issue PO PROC-4827, and
3) Process the first invoice on normal net-30 terms.

DocuSign (optional): https://app.docusign.com/prepare/XXXX-BlueHarbor-Setup

On Oct 16, 2028, Ana Ruiz <ana.ruiz@blueharbor-sys.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the note and the checklist. Please find attached our completed W-8BEN-E (scanned) and the certificate of incorporation.

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the attachments — I can confirm we received the two files. To answer your questions: 

- Redwood's standard is to have either a US EIN OR a government-issued foreign TIN supported by a government letter / official transcript. A scanned W-8BEN-E is helpful but we usually require the form to show an original signature (scan of the original) and for foreign TINs we ask for a corroborating document such as an HMRC letter or tax authority printout.
- Notarization is preferred if you expect to claim treaty benefits; if you do not claim treaty benefits and the TIN is present we can often proceed with a secondary verification (bank letter + incorporation cert) and move the PO forward subject to a final check.

For the interim PO request: we can open a provisional PO that allows you to submit an initial invoice for the onboarding fees provided we receive the HMRC confirmation or a notarized W-8BEN-E within 7 business days. If you cannot provide those, payment will be queued until documents are validated.

Next steps: 
1) Please upload the HMRC confirmation (or notarized form) to the portal link above.
2) If you'd like the provisional PO now, confirm by replying to this message and we'll route expedited review with AP.

Cc'd Kimberly for legal/FATCA classification guidance.

Thanks,
Olga

Hi Ana / Olga,

Adding a quick legal checklist to make sure the W-8BEN-E will pass our compliance checks: 

- W-8BEN-E must include a printed name and original signature of an authorized officer (not just an administrative preparer).
- FATCA chapter 3 status must be clearly indicated (e.g., Active NFFE, Passive NFFE, etc.).
- If claiming treaty benefits, indicate the treaty article and provide a valid foreign TIN alongside the treaty claim.
- Beneficial owner names must be consistent with incorporation documents; if different DBAs exist please provide an ownership declaration.
- If you provide a scanned form, include a separate signed authorization letter from the director confirming the signature is the company officer.

Checklist (please provide as items):
1) Notarized W-8BEN-E OR scanned W-8BEN-E + director authorization letter
2) HMRC confirmation letter (or equivalent foreign TIN evidence)
3) Certificate of incorporation (already provided)
4) Bank account confirmation (bank letter or recent statement with company name)

Attachment: signed_authority_template.docx (use this for a director authorization letter).

If you confirm you'll upload items 1–3 within 7 business days we'll accept a provisional PO and process the onboarding invoice.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Compliance
Redwood Inference
